subject: SLA proposal: uptime baseline, latency SLOs, and monthly credit sizing
messages:
From: James Porter <james.porter@acme.io>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Legal <legal@acme.io>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 9 Mar 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood SLA proposal: uptime baseline and credits

Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the routing/fallback behavior. We are starting to draft the contract language for a pilot and need to nail two items before sending this to procurement:

1) Uptime baseline: Acme prefers a 99.95% monthly availability commitment for the hosted API endpoints powering their customer-facing use case. If Redwood is comfortable with 99.95, please confirm.
2) Monthly service credits: Acme wants a simple, predictable credit schedule (not a complex banding matrix). Our starting ask is: credits equal to 10% of monthly fees for any month availability falls below 99.95 but above 99.5, and 25% for <99.5.
3) Latency SLO: our product team is asking for an average 95th-percentile tail latency of <500ms for the short-text generation route. If that's not feasible in Hosted, we need to understand routing to Dedicated with associated pricing delta.

I've attached our internal recommended wording and a simple credit calculator (monthly-credit-matrix.xlsx). Can you respond with what you can accept vs. where you'd like carveouts? If possible, include an exception path for scheduled maintenance windows.

Best,
James
James Porter
Head of Integrations, Acme Corp
attachments: SLA_draft_Acme_v2.pdf (annotated), monthly-credit-matrix.xlsx
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: James Porter <james.porter@acme.io>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Mar 2025 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood SLA proposal: uptime baseline and credits

James — thanks for the clear asks and the attachments. Quick summary of our position and a proposal to move to concrete language: 

- Uptime baseline: we can commit to 99.95% monthly availability for the Hosted API for standard production endpoints, provided you agree to the standard maintenance carveouts (we propose weekly maintenance windows of up to 2 hours per month, announced 72 hours in advance).
- Monthly credits: we're open to a simplified two-tier credit schedule but propose lower caps to keep potential exposure bounded. Proposed by Redwood:
  * Availability >= 99.95%: no credit
  * 99.5% <= Availability < 99.95%: credit = 5% of that month's fees (rather than 10%)
  * Availability < 99.5%: credit = 15% of that month's fees (rather than 25%)
  Cap: total credits capped at 60% of monthly fees per rolling 3-month period.
- Latency SLO: the 95th percentile <500ms is achievable for small generation payloads in Hosted for our standard small-instance routes, but it depends on concurrency and prompt length. If Acme expects sustained high concurrency or long-context requests, Dedicated will be the recommended path and we can provide a pricing addendum.

Next steps: If this sounds reasonable, I'll ask Legal to draft an SLA clause with the credit matrix and maintenance carveouts. Laura and Ben — looping you in for procurement/finance language and any adjustments on caps.

Thanks,
Rishi
Director, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, James Porter <james.porter@acme.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Acme Legal <legal@acme.io>
Date: Tue, 11 Mar 2025 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood SLA proposal: uptime baseline and credits

Thanks Rishi and James — a couple of clarifications from our side to speed procurement: 

- Maintenance carveouts: instead of "weekly maintenance windows of up to 2 hours per month" (which reads oddly), we propose: "Planned maintenance up to 2 hours per calendar month, scheduled with >=72 hours notice; such windows are excluded from availability calculations."
- Credit cap: Ben and I prefer a shorter exposure window — proposing the cap apply per single month (cap at 60% of that month's fees) rather than rolling 3-month accumulation. This keeps remediations simple for both teams.
- Double-trigger rule: we suggest credits are payable only when both (a) availability falls below threshold AND (b) Redwood has identified a remedial action that failed to restore service within the agreed TTR (time-to-repair) window. This prevents cascading credits for transient, self-remediating events.

James — if Acme agrees to the lower percentages and the single-month cap, we can give Legal a clean SLA clause to insert. Otherwise, we can prepare a redline version of your draft.

Laura
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: James Porter <james.porter@acme.io>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Mar 2025 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood SLA proposal: uptime baseline and credits

James — quick commercial note from finance:

- We can accept the 99.95% baseline and the proposed credit bands (Rishi's percentages) if Acme: (1) agrees to the single-month 60% cap, and (2) accepts the standard maintenance carveouts Laura reworded.
- For latency: if the 95th <500ms is a hard requirement, we should model projected monthly cost under Dedicated for the expected qps profile. I can run a delta analysis once we have a 30-day expected usage profile from your infra team.

If that sounds OK, I'm happy to mark the draft SLA as "commercially approved" and ask Legal to start the redline.

Best,
Ben Carter
Head of Finance, Customer Revenue
Redwood Inference
